errors.text_span: The chart contains nine slices, representing nine categories of stimuli.
errors.evidence: The chart shows seven categories/slices, not nine. The categories are: Intra-agency news article, Press Release, Draft/Other, Email, Organizational Report, Interview, and External News Article.
The value for “External News Article” is 15 out of 38, which is approximately 39.5%, not 15%. The description incorrectly uses the numerator of the fraction as the percentage.

errors.text_span: depicted in a light teal color
errors.evidence: The slice for “External News Article” is dark green, not light teal.
The value for “Draft/Other” is 9 out of 38, which is approximately 23.7%, not 9%. The description incorrectly uses the numerator of the fraction as the percentage.
The slice for “Draft/Other” is dark red. The orange slice corresponds to “Intra-agency news article”.

errors.text_span: “Article” represents 5% of the total and is shown in purple.
errors.evidence: There is no category in the chart named just “Article”. This seems to be a hallucinated category. Furthermore, no category is exactly 5% (5/38 is ~13.2%), and the purple slice is “Organizational Report” (2/38).
The value for “Email” is 5 out of 38, which is approximately 13.2%, not 5%. The description incorrectly uses the numerator of the fraction as the percentage.
The slice for “Email” is brown, not magenta. The slice that could be described as magenta/purple is “Organizational Report”.
The value for “Organizational Report” is 2 out of 38, which is approximately 5.3%, not 2%. The description incorrectly uses the numerator of the fraction as the percentage.
The slice for “Organizational Report” is light purple/lavender. The dark blue slice corresponds to “Interview”.
The value for “Interview” is 2 out of 38, which is approximately 5.3%, not 2%. The description incorrectly uses the numerator of the fraction as the percentage.
The slice for “Interview” is dark blue, not grey. There are no grey slices in the chart.
The labels on the chart are fractions (e.g., 15/38), not percentages.
The labels are displayed outside the donut chart, not within each slice.

errors.text_span: The segments appear ordered from largest to smallest in terms of size.
errors.evidence: The segments are not ordered by size. For example, the largest slice (15/38) is followed clockwise by a much smaller one (2/38).
The description omits two categories shown in the chart: “Intra-agency news article” (1/38) and “Press Release” (4/38).
The chart is a donut chart, which is a specific type of pie chart. While not a major error, being more specific would be better.
